extracted.intended_audience: H-1B petitioners and registrants (employers), immigration attorneys/representatives, and regulatory analysts
extracted.subtask_short: H-1B registration and selection weighting rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rule and guidance for electronic H-1B registrations (and petitions if registration suspended), specifying required registration information, how registrations are weighted/entered into selection pools by OEWS wage levels, and DHS methods for estimating burdens, costs, transfers, and economic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registration information (wage level, SOC code, area of employment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant will be required to select the box for the highest OEWS wage level ('wage level IV,' 'wage level III,' 'wage level II,' or 'wage level I') that the beneficiary’s proffered wage generally equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and in the area(s) of intended employment, and to provide the appropriate SOC code and area of intended employment that served as the basis for the OEWS wage level indicated on the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also must provide any other information required on the electronic registration form (and on the H-1B petition) as specified in the registration form instructions. Submission of additional wage level information and the SOC code on both an electronic registration and on Form I-129 will improve integrity of selection and adjudication processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage-level selection when prevailing wage not OEWS-based
rubrics_metrics.description: For registrants relying on a prevailing wage that is not based on the OEWS survey, if the proffered wage is less than the corresponding level I OEWS wage, the registrant will select the 'wage level I' box on the registration form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when prevailing wage source differs from OEWS; ensures conservative (lowest) classification when wage below OEWS level I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage-level selection for wage ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proffered wage is expressed as a range, the registrant will select the OEWS wage level that the lowest wage in the range will equal or exceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lowest point of any proffered wage range to determine the OEWS wage-level box to prevent overstating wage level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple locations or multiple positions (agent) — choose lowest equivalent wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: If the H-1B beneficiary will work in multiple locations, or in multiple positions if the registrant is an agent, the registrant will select the box for the lowest equivalent wage level among the corresponding wage levels for each of those locations or each of those positions and will list the location corresponding to that lowest equivalent wage level as the area of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision is meant to prevent gaming of the weighted selection process (e.g., listing a high-paying location or position for a small percent of time to increase selection chance). Note: listing the lowest-location at registration does not preclude listing additional concurrent work locations on the petition if selected and eligible to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance when OEWS wage data are not available
rubrics_metrics.description: In the limited instance where there is no current OEWS prevailing wage information for the proffered position, such that there are not four wage levels for the occupational classification or there are not wage data for the area of intended employment, the registrant will follow DOL guidance on Prevailing Wage Determinations (PWDs) to determine which OEWS wage level to select on the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS expects registrants will be able to identify the appropriate SOC code because petitioners must identify SOC codes on LCAs; use SOC code + DOL PWD guidance to determine OEWS wage level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of registrations into weighted selection pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations assigned wage level IV will be entered into the selection pool four times, those assigned wage level III will be entered three times, those assigned wage level II will be entered two times, and those assigned wage level I will be entered one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting increases odds of selection for registrations with proffered wages corresponding to higher OEWS wage levels; applies to registrations (or petitions if registration process suspended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique beneficiary counted only once toward numerical allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unique beneficiary will only be counted once toward the numerical allocation projections, regardless of how many registrations were submitted for that beneficiary or how many times the beneficiary is entered in the selection pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents double-counting of beneficiaries even if multiple registrations were submitted on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple registrations for same beneficiary are allotted to lowest wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: If a beneficiary has multiple registrations, the unique beneficiary will be allotted to the lowest wage level of all registrations submitted on his or her behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures conservative assignment if multiple registrations differ in indicated wage level; works together with the multiple-locations/positions rule to reduce gaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain two-stage selection process for advanced degree exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule will maintain the two-stage selection process (combined pool followed by selection to meet the advanced degree exemption) to keep a higher chance of beneficiaries with a qualifying U.S. master’s degree or higher of being selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analytical simplicity, DHS sometimes combines pools when comparing probabilities, but operationally the two-stage approach is retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting applies to registrations or petitions when registration suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule's weighting and selection based on OEWS wage levels applies to electronic registrations submitted for unique beneficiaries and also to petitions if the registration process is suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulatory text explicitly covers both registrations and petitions as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of LCA-derived wage-level distribution as proxy for registration distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS assumes that the H-1B cap-subject petition receipts percentages by wage levels from LCA data are predictive of the H-1B registrations percentages by wage levels and uses LCA wage level data as a reasonable proxy for registration wage level data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS acknowledges this may be an upper-bound if proffered wages exceed wage levels indicated on LCAs and that DHS cannot estimate how many registrants will select a higher wage level than required on the LCA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 5-year averages to estimate registration and petition populations
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS uses historical data of registrations and petitions and specifically uses 5-year averages to estimate the number of registrations and H-1B cap-subject petitions received annually (e.g., 5-year annual average receipts used for projections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS explains why it does not adjust these estimates for certain transient policies (e.g., an H-1B Proclamation) and notes limitations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of economic impacts considered (costs, transfers, benefits, distributional effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis distinguishes annualized monetized transfers and benefits (discounted at 3% and 7%), annualized unquantified monetized transfers, qualitative (unquantified) transfers, effects on State/local/Tribal governments, and effects on small businesses (Regulatory Flexibility Act analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include an unquantifiable producer-surplus transfer from petitioners hiring wage level I workers to petitioners hiring higher-wage workers; DHS reports both quantifiable and unquantifiable impacts and assesses small-entity impacts (e.g., estimate that final rule will result in a significant economic impact on 5,193 small entities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-burden estimate per registration and change calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the change will increase the time burden by 20 minutes for each registration (0.3333 hours) from 36 minutes (0.6 hours) to 56 minutes (0.9333 hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This increased burden reflects additional instructions and requirements (wage level box, SOC code, area of employment, passport/travel doc instructional language, and clarifying language on denying/revoking petitions). DHS multiplies time burdens by compensation rates to compute opportunity cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity-cost methodology and wage-rate assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: To estimate opportunity cost of time, DHS multiplies the estimated time burden by assumed preparer compensation rates: mean hourly wage of $36.57 for HR specialists, $84.84 for in-house lawyers; applies a benefits-to-wage multiplier of 1.45 to account for full employer cost of benefits; and uses a multiplier of 2.5 on in-house lawyer wages to approximate outsourced lawyer costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS assumes registrants may use HR specialists, in-house lawyers, or outsourced lawyers; it presents ranges and averages (e.g., assumes possible 50/50 split between in-house and outsourced lawyers) and reports resulting total opportunity-cost estimates for current and final burdens (tables with totals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of N/A wage-level data in historical tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Where historical H-1B cap-subject receipts have wage levels not available (N/A), DHS redistributes N/A counts among wage levels using the percent of total when estimating percentages by wage level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for level II redistribution, add proportional share of N/A counts based on level II's percent of total when computing 5-year averages and derived distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative integrity benefit from additional registration data
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS states that providing the area of intended employment, corresponding wage level, and SOC code on registration and petition will result in qualitative benefits by allowing USCIS to further improve the integrity of the H-1B cap selection and adjudication processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated as an unquantified qualitative benefit of the rule change in addition to quantified costs and transfers.
